hypothesis: Question: does the strong development result of the raw-target HistGradientBoosting reference (idea-baseline-2, action d81da712..., dev RMSE 59.99 vs Ridge 182.95 vs median 268.48) rest on relationships that transfer to a later period, or partly on a non-extrapolable level feature? Trees cannot extrapolate elapsed_day beyond the training range, and the raw-count target forces the model to learn hour-by-level interactions additively even though rental growth from 2011 to 2012 is plausibly multiplicative (hourly pattern scaled by a rising volume). Contrasting expected outcomes: (A) log1p target and/or dropping elapsed_day transfer better on a chronological internal holdout (last 61 training dates, future-period transfer rather than interpolation) and reduce negative bias on high-volume 2012 hours; (B) raw target wins because RMSE is dominated by peak hours and log fitting under-weights them, and elapsed_day helps by pinning the latest level via its last leaf. The program runs all 6 combinations, selects by internal holdout RMSE, refits on the full train set, and reports internal RMSE/MAE/bias, the selected branch, a 2012/2011 same-month level-ratio diagnostic, and any fallback use. Prior evidence changed my view only in that the Ridge->HGB gap shows nonlinear hour/weather structure is essential, so I keep the HGB core and vary only target scale and the trend feature. Note: early_stopping is set to False explicitly (the reference used sklearn's auto early stopping since train exceeds 10000 rows), so this is a joint change, not a one-factor attribution to the transform alone. Exploratory and unverified until executed.
